notes:
Profile: SMB customer building a chat-first support assistant integrated into Zendesk and Intercom. Primary ask: hosted API (self-serve) but need to understand limits and how platform behaves under sudden bursts from marketing/promotions.

What they told us / pain signals:
- 'We had a live demo where multiple agents joined and the app started returning 429s' (customer quote).
- Heavy short-lived spikes: expected pattern is many users opening chat after a promotional email; median session length ~80 tokens, but spikes produce many parallel requests.
- Want guidance on per-user vs account-wide concurrency, and best-effort strategies to avoid blocking customer agents during peak.

Technical targets and constraints:
- Latency target: p95 <= 300ms for single-turn replies; p50 ideally <150ms.
- Throughput: steady-state ~40 req/s, burst up to 500 concurrent short requests for ~20-60s during promos.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — will start small, needs predictable token pricing and burst capacity path.
- Model preference: lightweight Llama-style open variants (cost-conscious), but wants fallback to larger model only if latency/quality tradeoffs justify.

Key asks from Redwood during discovery:
- Clear rate limit/quota table and how 429s are signaled (headers, retry-after).
- Best-practice retry/backoff example for client SDKs and sample code to implement exponential backoff with jitter.
- How burst credit/temporary capacity is handled (auto-burst vs request to support).
- Visibility: need dashboard metrics for per-token spend, current concurrency, and quota remaining at account level and per-api-key.
- SLA questions: whether hosted tier offers soft fallback (queueing) or immediate 429s; what are recommended routing/fallback strategies.

POC plan agreed:
1) Redwood to provide: sample client that can emit the exact headers and interpret 429/retry-after, POC instructions to simulate marketing burst, and suggested SDK retry config.
2) Supportly to run: 3 incremental stress tests — low (50 rps), medium (150 rps), burst (simulate 500 concurrent short chats for 30s). Capture 429 rate, retry success, and end-to-end latency.
3) Joint review call to align on threshold tuning and recommend Dedicated path if predictable higher sustained throughput needed.

Open items / blockers:
- Need concrete per-account concurrency defaults and policies (how to request temporary increases).
- Dashboard prototype for quota headroom requested by SE.
- SSO SAML metadata pending from Supportly security team (blocks final security sign-off).

Action items assigned:
- Avery: share hosted API quota doc + JS client snippet by 2026-03-11.
- Priya (SE): prepare POC load script and monitoring hooks; coordinate INF-8721 updates.
- Supportly engineering: handoff IdP metadata and schedule POC run week of 2026-03-15.
